verses.zh: 亚希多弗又对押沙龙说：「求你准我挑选一万二千人，今夜我就起身追赶大卫，
verses.en: Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Let me pick out 12,000 men. Then I will go and pursue David this very night.
verses.commentary:
17:1 There are three cohortatives in this first verse.

- choose ‒ BDB 103, KB 119, Qal

- arise ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal

- pursue ‒ BDB 922, KB 1191, Qal

These are Ahithophel's first suggestions to Absalom. Ahithophel would lead 12,000 select troops
to immediately defeat David.

Surprisingly, Joesphus, Antiq. 7.9.6, has "10,000 chosen men." Numbers are often confused
in the way they are written in Hebrew.

verses.zh: 趁他疲乏手软，我忽然追上他，使他惊惶；跟随他的民必都逃跑，我就单杀王一人，
verses.en: When I catch up with[NOTE:1] him he will be exhausted and worn out.[NOTE:2] I will rout him, and the entire army that is with him will flee. I will kill only the king
notes: Heb “and I will come upon him.”
Heb “exhausted and slack of hands.”
verses.commentary:
17:2-3 Here is what he hopes will happen.

- come upon him while he is weary and exhausted

- he will be terrified and his supporters will flee

- Ahithophel will personally kill David

- all David's supporters will return to Absalom

- all Israelites will then seek peace (i.e., no civil war)

verses.zh: 使众民都归顺你。你所寻找的人既然死了，众民就如已经归顺你；这样，也都平安无事了。」
verses.en: and will bring the entire army back to you. In exchange for the life of the man you are seeking, you will get back everyone.[NOTE:1] The entire army will return unharmed.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “like the returning of all, the man whom you are seeking.” The LXX reads differently: “And I will return all the people to you the way a bride returns to her husband, except for the life of the one man whom you are seeking.” The other early versions also struggled with this verse. Modern translations are divided as well: the NAB, NRSV, REB, and NLT follow the LXX, while the NASB and NIV follow the Hebrew text.
Heb “all of the people will be safe.”
verses.commentary:
17:3 This verse is difficult to translate because the Hebrew is uncertain (JPSOA footnote). It seems to imply
that Absalom should kill only David and then his followers would return to Absalom as king of Israel.

See UBS Text Project, pp. 246-247 for details. It suggests that the MT is corrupt but also the LXX is
not original. The LXX has:

"and I will turn all the people back to you, as a bride turning back to her husband. You seek only the life of one man,
and there will be peace for all the people."

This LXX form is followed by NRSV, NJB, and REB.

Josephus, Antiq. 7.9.6, implies the promise is only to Absalom's fighting men.

verses.zh: 押沙龙和以色列的长老都以这话为美。
verses.en: This seemed like a good idea to Absalom and to all the leaders[NOTE:1] of Israel.
notes: Heb “elders.”

verses.zh: 押沙龙说：「要召亚基人户筛来，我们也要听他怎样说。」
verses.en: But Absalom said, “Call for[NOTE:1] Hushai the Arkite, and let’s hear what he has to say.”[NOTE:2]
notes: In the MT the verb is singular, but in the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate it is plural.
Heb “what is in his mouth.”

verses.zh: 户筛到了押沙龙面前，押沙龙向他说：「亚希多弗是如此如此说的，我们照着他的话行可以不可以？若不可，你就说吧！」
verses.en: So Hushai came to Absalom. Absalom said to him, “Here is what Ahithophel has advised. Should we follow his advice? If not, what would you recommend?”

verses.zh: 户筛对押沙龙说：「亚希多弗这次所定的谋不善。」
verses.en: Hushai replied to Absalom, “Ahithophel’s advice is not sound this time.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Not good is the advice which Ahithophel has advised at this time.”
verses.commentary:
17:7-14 This records Hushai's advice, as vv. 1-4 record Ahithophel's. The heart of Hushai's advice is "delay"
because David is a fierce military man and his warriors are valiant men. Wait until you can gather all Israelite conscripts
and attack in force. You personally must lead the force (v. 11).

This advice was from YHWH (v. 14).

17:7 "This time" Ahithophel was known for his wisdom (cf. 2 Sam. 16:23). So Hushai seems to acknowledge
this but suggests in this particular situation, perhaps there is a better idea.

verses.zh: 户筛又说：「你知道，你父亲和跟随他的人都是勇士，现在他们心里恼怒，如同田野丢崽子的母熊一般，而且你父亲是个战士，必不和民一同住宿。
verses.en: Hushai went on to say, “You know your father and his men—they are soldiers and are as dangerous as a bear out in the wild that has been robbed of her cubs.[NOTE:1] Your father is an experienced soldier; he will not stay overnight with the army.
notes: The LXX (with the exception of the recensions of Origen and Lucian) repeats the description as follows: “Just as a female bear bereft of cubs in a field.”
verses.commentary:
17:8-9 Notice how Hushai characterizes David and his men.

- they are mighty men, vv. 8,10

- they are fierce, like a bear robbed of her cubs (lit. "bitter of soul" for being run out of their homes in Jerusalem)

- David is an expert in warfare (lit. "man of war")

- they are valiant men, v. 10

verses.zh: 他现今或藏在坑中或在别处，若有人首先被杀，凡听见的必说：『跟随押沙龙的民被杀了。』
verses.en: At this very moment he is hiding out in one of the caves or in some other similar place. If it should turn out that he attacks our troops first,[NOTE:1] whoever hears about it will say, ‘Absalom’s army has been slaughtered!’
notes: Heb “that he falls on them [i.e., Absalom’s troops] at the first [encounter]; or “that some of them [i.e., Absalom’s troops] fall at the first [encounter].”
verses.commentary:
17:9-10 If only some of Absalom's troops are killed it would be discouraging to all the other troops
(i.e., lose heart). Because of David's experience in battle and the fighting ability of his men, causalities among
Absalom's troops would be likely.

verses.zh: 虽有人胆大如狮子，他的心也必消化；因为以色列人都知道你父亲是英雄，跟随他的人也都是勇士。
verses.en: If that happens even the bravest soldier—one who is lion-hearted—will virtually melt away. For all Israel knows that your father is a warrior and that those who are with him are brave.
verses.commentary:
17:10 "will completely lose heart" This is an intensified grammatical form (i.e., the INFINITIVE
ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB from the same root).

verses.zh: 依我之计，不如将以色列众人―从但直到别是巴，如同海边的沙那样多―聚集到你这里来，你也亲自率领他们出战。
verses.en: My advice therefore is this: Let all Israel from Dan to Beer Sheba—in number like the sand by the sea—be mustered to you, and you lead them personally into battle.
verses.commentary:
17:11 "be surely gathered" This is the same emphatic construction as v. 10.

▣ "from Dan even to Beersheba" These two cities, one in the far north of Canaan and one in southern
Judah, became an idiom for all of the Promised Land (cf. Jdgs. 20:1; 1 Sam. 3:20; 2 Sam. 3:10; 24:2,15).

▣ "as sand that is by the sea" This imagery is often used of military forces
(cf. Josh. 11:4; Jdgs. 7:12; 1 Sam. 13:5).

verses.zh: 这样，我们在何处遇见他，就下到他那里，如同露水下在地上一般，连他带跟随他的人，一个也不留下。
verses.en: We will come against him wherever he happens to be found. We will descend on him like the dew falls on the ground. Neither he nor any of the men who are with him will be spared alive—not one of them!

verses.zh: 他若进了哪一座城，以色列众人必带绳子去，将那城拉到河里，甚至连一块小石头都不剩下。」
verses.en: If he regroups in a city, all Israel will take up ropes to that city and drag it down to the valley, so that not a single pebble will be left there!”

verses.zh: 押沙龙和以色列众人说：「亚基人户筛的计谋比亚希多弗的计谋更好！」这是因耶和华定意破坏亚希多弗的良谋，为要降祸与押沙龙。
verses.en: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Arkite sounds better than the advice of Ahithophel.” Now the Lord had decided[NOTE:1] to frustrate the sound advice of Ahithophel, so that the Lord could bring disaster on Absalom.
notes: Heb “commanded.”
verses.commentary:
17:14 "For the Lord had ordained to thwart the good counsel of Ahithophel"
Human's plans are one thing but "the" thing is YHWH's will! He uses people to accomplish His plans (i.e., Exod. 3:7-10).

verses.zh: 户筛对祭司撒督和亚比亚他说：「亚希多弗为押沙龙和以色列的长老所定的计谋是如此如此，我所定的计谋是如此如此。
verses.en: Then Hushai reported to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, “Here is what Ahithophel has advised Absalom and the leaders[NOTE:1] of Israel to do, and here is what I have advised.
notes: Heb “elders.”
verses.commentary: 17:15-21 This describes the efforts of Zadok and Abiathar and their sons (v. 17) to inform David of Absalom's plans.

verses.zh: 现在你们要急速打发人去，告诉大卫说：『今夜不可住在旷野的渡口，务要过河，免得王和跟随他的人都被吞灭。』」
verses.en: Now send word quickly to David and warn him,[NOTE:1] “Don’t spend the night at the fords[NOTE:2] of the wilderness tonight. Instead, be sure you cross over,[NOTE:3] or else the king and everyone who is with him may be overwhelmed.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “send quickly and tell David saying.”

The MT reads “the rift valleys (עֲרָבוֹת, ʿaravot) of the wilderness.” The plural form typically refers to the gently sloping plains at the basin of the rift valley just north of the Dead Sea (while the larger rift valley extends from Galilee to the Gulf of Aqaba). Many translations render as the “fords” (NASB, ESV, NIV, NRSV) assuming the reversal of two letters as עֲבָרוֹת (ʿavarot, “fords, crossing”).
That is, “cross over the Jordan River.”
Heb “swallowed up.”
verses.commentary:
17:16 "but by all means cross over" This is an emphatic grammatical form (i.e., the INFINITIVE
ABSOLUTE and the IMPERFECT VERB from the same root).

▣

NASB, Peshitta
"destroyed"

NKJV, NRSV, LXX
"swallowed up"

TEV
"killed"

NJB, JPSOA
"annihilated"

The MT has the VERB (BDB 118, KB 134, Pual IMPERFECT)
which literally means "to swallow," "to engulf," which is an idiom for destruction. It views death as

- an animal with a large mouth (i.e., Jer. 51:34)

- the ground opening and the earth swallowing (i.e., descent into Sheol, cf. Exod. 15:12; Num. 16:30,32;
Deut. 11:6; Isa. 28:4)

verses.zh: 那时，约拿单和亚希玛斯在隐・罗结那里等候，不敢进城，恐怕被人看见。有一个使女出来，将这话告诉他们，他们就去报信给大卫王。
verses.en: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying in En Rogel. A female servant would go and inform them, and they would then go and inform King David. It was not advisable for them to be seen going into the city.

verses.zh: 然而有一个童子看见他们，就去告诉押沙龙。他们急忙跑到巴户琳某人的家里；那人院中有一口井，他们就下到井里。
verses.en: But a young man saw them on one occasion and informed Absalom. So the two of them quickly departed and went to the house of a man in Bahurim. There was a well in his courtyard, and they got down in it.
verses.commentary:
17:18 "a lad did see them and told Absalom" Again the actions of men cannot thwart the will of YHWH.
But notice He uses a man and a woman in Bahurim to accomplish His will.

Josephus, Antiq. 7.9.7, says "But certain horsemen saw them."

verses.zh: 那家的妇人用盖盖上井口，又在上头铺上碎麦，事就没有泄漏。
verses.en: His wife then took the covering and spread it over the top of the well and scattered some grain over it. No one was aware of what she had done.

verses.zh: 押沙龙的仆人来到那家，问妇人说：「亚希玛斯和约拿单在哪里？」妇人说：「他们过了河了。」仆人找他们，找不着，就回耶路撒冷去了。
verses.en: When the servants of Absalom approached the woman at her home, they asked, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman replied to them, “They crossed over the stream.” Absalom’s men[NOTE:1] searched but did not find them, so they returned to Jerusalem.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they”; the referents (Absalom’s men) have been specified in the translation for clarity.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
17:20

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"the brook of water"

TEV
"the river"

NJB
"towards the water"

REB
"past the pool"

JPSOA
"a bit beyond the water"

Targum
"the Jordan"

LXX
"a little way from the water"

Peshitta
"they wanted water"

NET
"the stream"

The NOUN (BDB 568, KB 576) occurs only here.

- BDB ‒ "brook," "stream"

- KB ‒ "collection," "container"

In context it seems to refer to the Jordan River (Targums).

verses.zh: 他们走后，二人从井里上来，去告诉大卫王说：「亚希多弗如此如此定计害你，你们务要起来，快快过河。」
verses.en: After the men had left, Ahimaaz and Jonathan[NOTE:1] climbed out of the well. Then they left and informed King David. They advised David, “Get up and cross the stream[NOTE:2] quickly, for Ahithophel has devised a plan to catch you.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “they”; the referents (Ahimaaz and Jonathan) have been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “the water.”

Heb “for thus Ahithophel has devised against you.” The expression “thus” is narrative shorthand, referring to the plan outlined by Ahithophel (see vv. 1-3). The men would surely have outlined the plan in as much detail as they had been given by the messenger.

verses.zh: 于是大卫和跟随他的人都起来，过约旦河。到了天亮，无一人不过约旦河的。
verses.en: So David and all the people who were with him got up and crossed the Jordan River.[NOTE:1] By dawn there was not one person left who had not crossed the Jordan.
notes: The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text here or in v. 24, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 亚希多弗见不依从他的计谋，就备上驴，归回本城；到了家，留下遗言，便吊死了，葬在他父亲的坟墓里。
verses.en: When Ahithophel realized that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey and returned to his house in his hometown. After setting his household in order, he hanged himself. So he died and was buried in the grave[NOTE:1] of his father.
notes: The Greek recensions of Origen and Lucian have here “house” for “grave.”
verses.commentary:
17:23 Ahithophel realized that Absalom's actions would result in defeat. So he went home and took his own life.
Suicide in the OT, mostly connected with warfare, was not condemned (i.e., Jdgs. 9:54; 1 Sam. 31:5; 1 Kgs. 16:18).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SUICIDE

▣ "buried in the grave of his father" This would refer to a family burial place (i.e., a cave, a special field).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEOL

verses.zh: 大卫到了玛哈念，押沙龙和跟随他的以色列人也都过了约旦河。
verses.en: Meanwhile David had gone to Mahanaim, while Absalom and all the men of Israel had crossed the Jordan River.

verses.zh: 押沙龙立亚玛撒作元帅，代替约押。亚玛撒是以实玛利人（又作以色列人）以特拉的儿子。以特拉曾与拿辖的女儿亚比该亲近；这亚比该与约押的母亲洗鲁雅是姊妹。
verses.en: Absalom had made Amasa general in command of the army in place of Joab. (Now Amasa was the son of an Israelite man named Jether, who had married[NOTE:1] Abigail the daughter of Nahash and sister of Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.)
notes: Heb “come to.”
verses.commentary:
17:25

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta
"the Israelite"

NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB
"the Ishmaelite"

The MT has "Israelite." Some LXX MSS have "Israelite"; others "the Ishmaelite." The confusion comes
from 1 Chr. 2:17, where this man is called "Jether the Ishmaelite." The UBS Text Project, p. 248, gives the MT a "B" rating
(some doubt).

▣ "Nahash" Again, there is some question about the name because of a reference in 1 Chr. 2:13-17, where
he is called "Jesse." The UBS Text Project, p. 248, gives the MT a "D" rating (highly doubtful).

verses.zh: 押沙龙和以色列人都安营在基列地。
verses.en: The army of Israel[NOTE:1] and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.
notes: Heb “and Israel.”

verses.zh: 大卫到了玛哈念，亚扪族的拉巴人拿辖的儿子朔比，罗・底巴人亚・米利的儿子玛吉，基列的罗基琳人巴西莱，
verses.en: When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Makir the son of Ammiel from Lo Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim
verses.commentary:
17:27 As Ziba had brought supplies for David and his men, family, and servants, so too, these others brought
abundant supplies to David at Mahanaim.

- Shobi (possibly the king of the Ammonites who replaced Hanum by David's command)

- Machir (helped Mephibosheth, cf. 2 Sam. 9:45)

- Barzillai (a friend of David's, cf. 2 Samuel 19)

In these days the armies were supplied by local residents.

verses.zh: 带着被、褥、盆、碗、瓦器、小麦、大麦、麦面、炒谷、豆子、红豆、炒豆、
verses.en: brought bedding, basins, and pottery utensils. They also brought food for David and all who were with him, including wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils,[NOTE:1]
notes: The MT adds “roasted grain” וְקָלִי (veqali) at the end of v. 28, apparently accidentally repeating the word from its earlier occurrence in this verse. With the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and an Old Latin ms the translation deletes this second occurrence of the word.

verses.zh: 蜂蜜、奶油、绵羊、奶饼，供给大卫和跟随他的人吃；他们说：「民在旷野，必饥渴困乏了。」
verses.en: honey, curds, flocks, and cheese.[NOTE:1] For they said, “The people are no doubt hungry, tired, and thirsty there in the desert.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “cheese of the herd,” probably referring to cheese from cow’s milk (rather than goat’s milk).
Or “wilderness” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV, TEV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
17:29

NASB, NKJV, NRSV
"curds, sheep, and cheese of the herd"

TEV
"cheese, cream and some sheep"

NJB
"curds, and cow's cheese and sheep's cheese"

REB
"curds, sheep and fat cattle"

JPSOA footnote
"curds from the flock"

LXX
"butter and sheep and saphphoth (cheese) from cows"

Peshitta
"butter and sheep and cheese from cows"

The question is, does this series of items refer to

- milk products and meat

- diary products only

I think #2 fits the list best. Sheep would not be listed between curds and cow cheese.

- Explain 2 Sam. 17:3 in your own words.

- How did Hushai's plan of attack differ from Ahithophel's?

- Is suicide a special sin? Does it separate one from God?

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 17:1-4

1Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Please let me choose 12,000 men that I may arise and pursue
David tonight. 2I will come upon him while he is weary and exhausted and terrify him, so that all the people
who are with him will flee. Then I will strike down the king alone, 3and I will bring back all the people to you.
The return of everyone depends on the man you seek; then all the people will be at peace." 4So the
plan pleased Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
